notes:
Account background:
- Mid-market SaaS (product analytics platform) planning to embed LLM features across product and support flows. CTO & Head of Product sponsoring.

Evaluation history (concise timeline):
- 2025-11-20: Intro call (Alex) — discussed high-level architecture, use-cases, compliance needs. Customer: "priority = predictable latency & cost".
- 2025-12-08: Hosted API trial started (10k free credits). SE (Priya) provided quickstart.
- 2026-01-12: Hosted demo: chat + reranking pipeline with sample traffic; latency 90th pctl ~180ms for short chat.
- 2026-01-25: Hosted POC metrics review — saw acceptable quality but cost projection at scale looked high (~$0.07/token-equivalent for heavy rerank workloads).
- 2026-02-18: Dedicated POC kickoff (on-prem-like VPC config). Fireflies: ff_2026-02-18_brookhaven-demo (link).
- 2026-02-26: Dedicated demo w/ batching + KV caching engaged. Throughput target hit: sustained 1,800 QPS internal test; p95 latency target 250ms under realistic concurrency.
- 2026-03-02: Pricing workshop w/ finance + product. Redwood presented three commit tiers + burst/overage model.

Use-case & requirements summary:
- Primary workloads: multitenant support-bot (low-latency chat), nightly reranking of candidate content (high throughput), document search embedding refresh.
- Latency targets: chat p95 <= 250ms, initial throughput for reranking 2k QPS (batchable) with spikes up to 5k QPS.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-high; CFO pushing for committed discounts vs pay-as-you-go.
- Model preferences: happy to use curated open models; want option to pin model version. Need fallback to smaller/cheaper variant during capacity events.
- Routing/fallback: require policy to route to cheaper regional pool first, failover to larger model as last resort.
- Security: must support SSO/SAML, SOC2, customer-managed KMS, audit logs retained 1 year, and contract language for US data residency.

Dedicated pricing/packaging negotiation notes (details):
- Redwood proposal v3 (presented 2026-03-02):
  * Commit tiers (monthly vCPU-equivalent/GPU-hours basis): Bronze (baseline) 3 units, Silver 8 units, Gold 16 units.
  * Burst allowance: 2x baseline for short bursts (first 30s window) included, 4x allowed for queued bursts with warmup fees.
  * Overage rate: staged overage per unit-hour after burst quota; baseline proposed $1.25/unit-hr overage, finance pushing to $0.75.
  * Ramp schedule: 6-month ramp recommended — commit floor increases at month 3 and month 6 tied to usage true-up.
  * Minimum contract term: 12 months with quarterly reviews; 30-day termination for material SLA breach only.
  * True-up cadence: quarterly by default; customer requesting monthly true-ups with cap on unexpected charges.
  * Support & SLA: 99.9% uptime target, 30ms median added latency SLA; premium on-call option for enterprise hours.

Customer counterpoints & asks:
- CFO asks for a lower starting commit (Gold too big); wants Silver + option to scale to Gold after 90 days rather than fixed ramp.
- Requests explicit burst credits (in tokens/units) rather than multiplier-based bursts. Wants guaranteed 60-minute emergency burst window once per quarter.
- Asks to cap overage per month to 20% of committed spend and negotiate a stepped price: first 20% at $0.90/unit-hr, above that $1.15.
- Wants monthly true-ups and a smoothing clause to avoid one-time big invoices during early usage ramp.
- Legal needs a KMS appendix and explicit data residency language for US-only processing in contract.

POC results (technical):
- Dedicated POC reduced cost-per-rerank by ~45% vs hosted projections when batching and KV caching used.
- Observed warmup time for cold KV caches: ~12s on large sessions; customer requests improved cache prewarm guidance in runbook.
- Model quality: equivalent scoring on core rerank testset; small hallucination issues in long-context summarization flagged for further prompt engineering.

Risks & blockers (operational):
- Pricing mismatch: finance and procurement negotiating internal approvals.
- Legal: KMS/data residency annex needs sign-off; redlines expected.
- Technical: customer wants deterministic failover behavior documented for multi-region routing.

Next steps (tactical):
- 2026-03-08: SE + customer to finalize sizing worksheet and select commit tier (Priya leading).
- 2026-03-12: Pricing finalization meeting w/ finance (Alex + Redwood pricing lead).
- 2026-03-18: Legal to exchange contract redlines (Jordan Lee to coordinate).
- Short-term ask: provide a 30-day pilot discount for Silver tier with explicit burst credits and monthly true-up demo PO.

Sales notes (tone):
- Buyer sentiment: pragmatic, cost-conscious but receptive to technical wins from Dedicated POC.
- "If we get predictable billing and the burst guarantees, we'll sign" — Head of Product (paraphrase).
- Priorities: lock down commit level that allows them to show CFO predictable monthly spend and avoid surprise overages.

Attachments: pricing deck, POC runbook, hosted POC metrics spreadsheet (links above).
